questions.text: Why does scaled dot-product attention divide query–key scores by the square root of the key dimension?

options.A: To make every token receive the same attention weight.
options.B: To prevent the value vectors from changing dimension.
options.C: To remove the need for learned query and key projections.
options.D: To limit score growth that can cause softmax saturation.

questions.explanation: As key dimension increases, unscaled dot products tend to grow in magnitude. Scaling helps avoid overly peaked softmax distributions and very small gradients.

questions.text: You are adding causal masking so each token can attend only to itself and earlier tokens. What should happen to scores for future positions?

options.A: Set them to zero after the softmax, without renormalizing.
options.B: Set them to negative infinity before applying softmax.
options.C: Set them to positive infinity before applying softmax.
options.D: Set their corresponding value vectors to all ones.

questions.explanation: Negative infinity before softmax gives future positions zero probability while normalizing over allowed positions.
